summary.title: Metabolic rescue assay draft with unit hygiene risks

findings.message: 370 C is outside a plausible wet-lab manuscript temperature range.
findings.evidence: A draft assay note says the plate was heated to 370 C for 15 min.
findings.recommendation: Confirm whether this is a typo, a specialized protocol condition, or a missing decimal point.

findings.message: metformin uses both molar and mass concentration units.
findings.recommendation: Add a molecular-weight conversion note or standardize the manuscript to one concentration basis.

findings.message: Numeric value "12,000" appears without an adjacent unit in Methods: cell culture and dosing.
findings.evidence: Pellets were centrifuged at 12,000 for 10 min before lysis.
findings.recommendation: Add the intended unit or rewrite the sentence so the quantity is unambiguous.

findings.message: TNF-alpha cell unit ng/mL does not match header unit pg/mL.
findings.evidence: Table 1. Inflammation marker summary, row 1, column "TNF-alpha (pg/mL)": 0.09 ng/mL
findings.recommendation: Convert the cell value to the header unit or split the column by unit.

findings.message: IL-6 cell unit ng/mL does not match header unit pg/mL.
findings.evidence: Table 1. Inflammation marker summary, row 2, column "IL-6 (pg/mL)": 0.21 ng/mL
findings.recommendation: Convert the cell value to the header unit or split the column by unit.

findings.message: Numeric value "35" appears without an adjacent unit in Results: cytokine response.
findings.evidence: ATP increased by 35 compared with vehicle control.
findings.recommendation: Add the intended unit or rewrite the sentence so the quantity is unambiguous.

findings.message: IL-6 is reported in multiple unit scales: pg/mL, ng/mL.
findings.evidence: results-cytokines: 180 pg/mL; results-cytokines: 0.22 ng/mL; table-cytokines: 180 pg/mL; table-cytokines: 0.21 ng/mL
findings.recommendation: Keep the source units if scientifically useful, but include a normalized value for reviewer comparison.

findings.message: TNF-alpha is reported in multiple unit scales: ng/mL, pg/mL.
findings.recommendation: Keep the source units if scientifically useful, but include a normalized value for reviewer comparison.
